question: can i use tools inside a batch request or is that only for the normal endpoint
supported_answer: Tools work in batches. Almost any Messages API request can be batched, explicitly including tool use and all server tools, and requests are processed independently so types can be mixed within one batch.

evidence.quote:
Almost any request you can make to the Messages API can be included in a batch. This includes:

* Vision
* Tool use, including all [server tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools) (web search, web fetch, code execution, MCP connectors, advisor, and tool search)
Because each request in the batch is processed independently, you can mix different types of requests within a single batch.

atomic_claims: tool use, including all server tools, can be included in a batch
each request in a batch is processed independently, so request types can be mixed
reasoning_type: membership check against a documented list
ambiguity_notes: A small number of Messages API parameters are unsupported in batches and return a validation error; that exclusion list is adjacent and is not contradicted by this answer.
verifier_notes: The independence span is included because the asker's implicit worry is whether batching constrains request shape.

question: what's the max number of requests in one batch job and how long till results expire
supported_answer: 100,000 requests or 256 MB, whichever comes first. Batches expire if processing does not finish within 24 hours, and results stay available for download for 29 days after creation.

evidence.quote: * A Message Batch is limited to either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB in size, whichever is reached first.

* The system processes each batch as fast as possible, with most batches completing within 1 hour. You can access batch results when all messages have completed or after 24 hours, whichever comes first. Batches expire if processing does not complete within 24 hours.
* Batch results are available for 29 days after creation.

batches expire if processing does not complete within 24 hours
batch results are available for 29 days after creation
ambiguity_notes: The question conflates two expiries — processing expiry and result retention. The corpus documents both and the answer keeps them distinct.
verifier_notes: Three spans because the question has two parts and the second part has two different documented meanings.

question: how many images can go in a single message and is there a size cap per image
supported_answer: Up to 100 images per API request on 200k-context models and 600 on others (20 per message on claude.ai). Maximum dimensions are 8000x8000 px, and the per-image size cap is 10 MB base64 on the Claude API directly.

* 20 per message on [claude.ai](https://claude.ai/).

* 600 per request on the API, for all other models.

The maximum size per image is:

* 10 MB (base64-encoded) when using the Claude API directly.

the per-image size cap is 10 MB base64 on the Claude API

question: resize images before sending? whats the point where it stops helping
supported_answer: The threshold is the model's maximum native resolution. Images larger than the long-edge or visual-token limit are downscaled before processing, so resizing above that point buys nothing. Below it, cost scales with size: an image costs ⌈width/28⌉ × ⌈height/28⌉ visual tokens.

evidence.quote: Each model has a maximum native image resolution, expressed as a long-edge limit and a visual-token limit. Images larger than either limit are downscaled before processing

Claude views images in patches instead of pixels. Each patch is a 28×28-pixel block of the image, referred to as a visual token. An image, therefore, costs `⌈width / 28⌉ × ⌈height / 28⌉` visual tokens.

atomic_claims: images larger than the long-edge or visual-token limit are downscaled before processing
an image costs ceil(width/28) x ceil(height/28) visual tokens
reasoning_type: identifying a threshold from a documented automatic behaviour plus a cost formula
ambiguity_notes: The corpus does not phrase this as advice about when resizing stops helping; it states the downscale rule and the cost formula, which together determine the point. Both are cited so the reasoning is visible rather than asserted.
verifier_notes: The formula span is what makes the answer actionable below the threshold; the downscale span is what makes it moot above.
